speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Education given that problematic gaming intersects mental health, education, student welfare and youth social development (a) whether the Ministry can elaborate on the current framework for cross-ministry coordination on this issue; and (b) whether preventive policy has emerged as a joint strategic priority.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The inter-agency efforts indeed span from preventive education to intervention and treatment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
text: MOE's Cyber Wellness lessons for primary to pre-university students teach the importance of maintaining a healthy balance of online and offline activities, and guide students to be discerning users of technology.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
text: This includes learning to manage their use of social media and online games, to recognise risks in the digital space and to manage negative influences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Beyond schools, we recognise that parents, too, play a critical role in guiding their children at home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
text: These include recognising the signs of excessive gaming, for example, increased levels of anxiety and excessive in-app purchases; and working with their child to counter excessive gaming by engaging in screen-free activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Relevant content of the guide is reinforced through MOE's Cyber Wellness lessons and also shared with parents.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As a parent of five kids, I can attest that gaming is indeed very addictive for school-going children.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Once they are given the devices and screens, they can be gaming for hours.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I just have two short supplementary questions, which are: can I clarify that MOE is indeed the lead agency involved because there are many Ministries involved in this area and MOE has clear lead ownership and outcome accountability on this particular issue?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And has the Government engaged gaming platforms on addictive design features?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: Indeed, as parents, many of us are concerned about the impact of gaming on the development of the child.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: With regard to the nature of addressing problematic gaming, indeed, it is a multi-agency approach which I have shared earlier.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: While MOE focuses on the preventive aspect towards encouraging our students having proper habits in engaging with the online space, you find that we take a calibrated approach to the level according to the age of the students.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: For example, at the primary levels, we nurture our students to learn good habits in terms of safe online practices and respectful online relationships.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: At secondary school, we look at learning about safety and empathy in relating to others, both online and offline.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: And in the post-secondary levels, we focus on the skills that are reinforced as students learn about cyber ethics, cyber citizenship and the positive role that they can play in the digital future.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: In terms of where they require subsequent care, certainly MOE works with the different partners and it takes a "many helping hands" approach.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: That is why, also in terms of the engagement with our colleagues from MOH, when it comes to the mental healthcare of the students who have problematic gaming in the mental wellness space, that is where we have partnerships as well.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: As to the Member's question about whether MOE is indeed the lead agency, it really takes a "many helping hands" approach because the issue spans quite broadly, throughout society, as well as the interface that we have with the challenges online.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: The Member's third question is actually subsumed in the last part of my reply.
